Subject: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate | Spaarne Gasthuis, Haarlem | 15 January 2025

Reason for Examination: 82-year-old gentleman presenting with a PSA value of 7.5 ng/mL; clinical query regarding a previously confirmed positive prostate biopsy.

FINDINGS:
Glandular volume measures 68.0 mL. Asymmetric enlargement of the prostate is evident. A discrete focal abnormality sits at the 12 o'clock position within the left basal peripheral zone, spanning roughly 14 x 11 mm. Signal characteristics show marked T2 hypointensity, restricted diffusion across elevated b-value DWI sequences, and prompt focal enhancement following dynamic contrast administration. Capsular integrity remains intact with no extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion. Pelvic lymph nodes exhibit normal size and morphology.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left basal peripheral zone.
PSAD: 0.11 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.71243304.
